items.title: From Waste Picker to Entrepreneur
items.summary: 05 OCT 2026 3:28PM by PIB Delhi Financial assistance and access to sustainable livelihood opportunities can play an important role in empowering individuals from disadvantaged communities and improving their socio-economic condition. Support for self-employment and mechanisation can help vulnerable workers move towards more stable sources of income, strengthen family financial security and promote dignity of work.

facts.text: Ms. Mekala Nancharamma , aged 30, belongs to the Scheduled Tribe (ST) community and has been working as a waste picker in the Guntur Municipal Corporation for nearly 12 years.
The total project cost was ₹16,99,952, comprising a loan of ₹10,24,964 and a capital subsidy of ₹6,74,988.
With the help of the mechanised equipment, she began earning an additional ₹ 10,000 per month .
Her monthly income, which was approximately ₹ 8,000 before the intervention, has increased to around ₹ 18,000 .

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 4 Geography › D-2 › Andhra Pradesh - climate, rainfall regions, cyclone vulnerability, drought-prone areas › Rain-shadow and drought-prone zone
bullets: Rayalaseema lies in the rain shadow of the Western Ghats and the Karnataka/Telangana highlands, so it gets little SW-monsoon rain (CDI). Anantapur is the lowest-rainfall district.
Chronic droughts hit Rayalaseema and southern Prakasam when the NE monsoon fails; groundwater depletion adds to this (CDI).

2026: a deficient year. The SW monsoon deficit reached 51.2% (1 Jun-25 Aug), with all 28 districts deficient. Causes: El Nino subsidence, and all seven low-pressure systems forming at the head of the Bay (CDCA Aug 2026).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 4 Geography › D-2 › India - rainfall distribution, variability, El Nino linkage, drought and flood-prone areas › Drought-prone areas - thresholds, share of land, chronic regions
bullets: About 68% of India's agricultural (cultivable) land is drought-prone in varying degrees (PYQ 2023 key).
Chronic drought: western India - Rajasthan, Gujarat (PYQ 2025), rain-shadow Deccan; in AP Rayalaseema and south Prakasam (NE monsoon failure + groundwater depletion) (CDI).
Types: meteorological (rain deficit), agricultural (soil moisture), hydrological (river/groundwater), flash drought (sudden heat + no rain) (LENS Jun 2025).

Manual for Drought Management (2016, revised 2020) uses rainfall deficit, vegetation, soil moisture and water indicators for declaration [GK]. Not in your sources: exact trigger thresholds of the current Manual.

items.title: Union Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers Anupriya Patel Launches 14th Edition of India Chem 2026
items.summary: The event will be held in Mumbai from October 22 to 24, 2026. Addressing the launch event in New Delhi, Smt. Anupriya Patel said that the Government is committed to creating a conducive ecosystem and strengthening infrastructure for the industry to make India self-reliant and realise the vision of a developed India by 2047.

facts.text: She further stated that the Department is already pursuing the Department of Science and Technology to declare chemicals and petrochemicals as a priority sector so that it will be covered under the new Research Development Innovation Scheme (RDI) which has an outlay of about 1 lakh Crores.
India Chem 2026 is being hosted by the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals in partnership with the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI).

The 14th edition of the biennial event will comprise an international exhibition and conference, bringing together key stakeholders from the chemicals and petrochemicals sector, including industry leaders, policymakers, investors, researchers and international participants.

bullets: Supreme Court Judges are governed under Part V, Chapter IV of the Constitution.
The Governor has no power to appoint High Court Judges.
A distinguished jurist is eligible for appointment as a Supreme Court Judge under Article 124(3)(c).
The President transfers High Court Judges on the advice of a collegium led by the Chief Justice of India.

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-2 › High Courts and subordinate judiciary; judicial review, judicial activism, PIL and judicial overreach debate › High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt
bullets: Under Art. 217, the President appoints after consulting the CJI and the Governor, and for puisne judges also the HC Chief Justice. Proposals start with the HC Chief Justice and the HC collegium (CJ + 2), then go to the SC collegium (CJI + 2 senior-most judges) (LENSD 12 Aug 2026).
The inquiry report on Yashwant Varma (formerly Allahabad HC) was to be tabled despite his resignation (LENSD 11 Jul 2026).

Contempt: Arts. 129 and 215 make the SC and HCs courts of record. The Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 followed the H.N. Sanyal Committee and defines civil contempt (wilful disobedience) and criminal contempt (scandalising or obstructing justice). Fair criticism and accurate reporting are exceptions (VIS 2026).
Art. 215: every HC is a court of record; punishes contempt of itself and subordinate courts (SC: Art. 129).

Appellate: primarily a court of appeal; second civil appeals on questions of law only; death sentences of Sessions Courts need HC confirmation (now under BNSS 2023, which replaced CrPC from 1 July 2024) .

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-2 › Governor - appointment, powers, discretionary powers, position and controversies (Article 200/201, Article 356 reports) › Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)
bullets: Art. 155: appointed by the President by warrant under hand and seal. The Governor is neither directly nor indirectly elected.

The term is 5 years, but he continues until his successor enters office . So "quits office immediately after the term expires" is the wrong statement (APPSC-G1 2019). He resigns to the President, may be transferred, and may be reappointed.

In B.P. Singhal v. UoI (2010), the pleasure doctrine is not unfettered: a Governor cannot be removed arbitrarily or merely because the Centre's government changes, and removal is open to limited judicial review . No grounds for removal are stated in the Constitution.
Grounds for removal are not stated in the Constitution. The President may transfer a Governor, and a Governor may be reappointed (APP).

Art 200 reservation: mandatory for bills endangering the High Court's position (APP; IYB). The President has an absolute veto over reserved bills (APP). APPSC 2025 key: reservation is an example of central control over states.

items.title: CAQM intensifies field-level monitoring with deployment of Flying Squads to prevent paddy stubble burning incidents in Punjab and Haryana
items.summary: 05 OCT 2026 7:33PM by PIB Delhi The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) has further intensified its coordinated field-level monitoring mechanism for prevention and control of paddy stubble burning incidents in Punjab and Haryana.

facts.text: The deployment covers 18 districts in Punjab and 16 districts in Haryana, providing extensive field-level monitoring across the two States during the critical paddy harvesting period.

The teams will coordinate with farmers, Parali Protection Force, district-level authorities, State Government Nodal Officers, officers of the respective State Pollution Control Boards, CAQM Cell at SAS Nagar and the Commission.

The Commission has reiterated the need for concerted efforts by all concerned agencies, along with active facilitation and cooperation of farmers and other stakeholders, to ensure prevention of stubble burning during the season.

bullets: AP farmers borrow from commercial banks, RRBs and PACS, i.e. all of them (PYQ 2008). Other formal sources are SHGs/JLGs, microfinance and KCC.
Nationally, scheduled commercial banks give over 70% of formal farm credit. The cooperative system (PACS-DCCB-SCB) gives short-term credit, and ARDBs give long-term credit (LENS Apr 2026).
AP Annual Credit Plan 2025-26 review (Jan 2026): Rs 2.96 lakh crore disbursed to agriculture and allied sectors, Rs 1,490 crore to tenant farmers and Rs 95,714 crore to MSMEs (TH, 24 Jan 2026).
Formal credit excludes many tenant, tribal, women and oral-lessee farmers because it needs land records. A NABARD Guntur study found formal interest rates of about 2.5-10%.
KCC (1998, NABARD model scheme on the R.V. Gupta Committee): RBI's revised KCC Directions of 19 Jun 2026 apply to loans from 1 Jan 2027, with a maximum tenure of 6 years (earlier 5).

bullets: Sea level: thermal expansion plus ice melt; uninhabited South Pacific islets Tebua Tarawa and Abanuea submerged in 1999; Kiribati, Tuvalu at risk (APP).

Coral bleaching: the 1.2 degC threshold for large-scale warm-water reef collapse is already crossed; beyond ~2 degC parts of the Amazon may turn savanna (UN brief, LENSD 24 Jun 2026). Reefs need 15+ years to recover (APP).
Oceans and species: acidity up 30% since the Industrial Revolution (CDI); up to 25% of mountain species face extinction (AR6, CDI).

Extremes and agriculture: India 2025 - 4,419 deaths and 17.4 million ha of crops damaged by extreme weather (WMO 2025, CDI); buffalo milk yields in Haryana's trans-Gangetic plains hit by warming (TH, 6 Jul 2026).
Disease spread: warmer, wetter conditions widen the range of vector-borne diseases such as malaria and dengue.

2025 = International Year of Quantum Science and Technology (UN; centenary of quantum mechanics) ; World Quantum Day = 14 April.

Women's reservation in the House of the People covers seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Women's reservation in the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi covers Scheduled Caste-reserved seats.
Not less than one-third of the total seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes under Article 243D(2) must be reserved for women belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
The mandatory sub-quota for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe women within Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe reserved seats is one-third.

Article 46 provides for the promotion of Scheduled Caste interests.
